title: Industrial Flex Space Savoy, IL
description: Department/Ind. Agency US DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION Sub-tier FEDERAL AVIATION ADMINISTRATION Office 697DCM Classification Original Set Aside (blank) Product Service Code X1GZ-LEASE/RENTAL OF OTHER WAREHOUSE BUILDINGS Place NAICS Code 531120 - Lessors of Nonresidential Buildings (except Miniwarehouses) Place of Performance INSERT THE MAJOR CITY IN THE SEARCH AREA Initiative Savoy, IL Description The U.S. Department of Transportation, Federal Aviation Administration is seeking competitive lease proposals for industrial flex space in Support of Federal Aviation Administration field operations. Delineated Area: North: E Leverett Road East: IL�130 South: County Road 700 N West: S Staley Road Buildings that have frontage on the boundary streets are deemed to be within the delineated Area of Consideration. Buildings outside of the search area will not be considered. Lease Term: 10 years (see Government termination rights in the draft lease paragraph TERMINATION FOR CONVENIENCE) Space Requirements Minimum ABOA RSF: 5,374 Maximum ABOA RSF: 6,374 Space shall be contiguous on the same floor. Requests to be on the 1st floor (see section H of Requirements document) Three enclosed offices (each 150 sq. ft.) 12 workstations office (each 8x8) Technical Administrative Space SSC CBI Room (150 SF) SSC Conference Room (w/ Special A/V) (300 SF) SSC NAS Documentation Area (100 SF) SSC PPE Storage � Personal (56 SF) SSC Secure Storage (200 SF) SSC Security Equipment Room (50 SF) SSC Technical/Electronics Workshop (300 SF) SSC Telco Room/Space/LAN Space (50 SF) Technical Shop Space (890 SF) SSC PPE Storage � Group (150 SF) SSC Shipping/Receiving (140 SF) SSC Supply/Parts Room (600 SF) 24-Hour Access: The FAA requires access to the space 24 hours per day / 7 days a week. Loading Dock: If the space offered is above ground level, the FAA requires a freight elevator that can accommodate small cart to transport supplies, records, etc. HVAC: The FAA requires dedicated 24/7 HVAC operation in IT and LAN room. Temperature in the IT and LAN room is per OSHA requirements. Overtime Utilities: The FAA requires utilities to be available when personnel are working within the space. Ceiling Height: Admin and shop space is the standard 9'ft. The Government requires 10 overnight parking spaces for GOVs. They may need to be secured depending on FAA security inspection and crime cast score and 15 general outside parking spaces, reserved for the exclusive use of the Government. Offeror must include the cost of this parking as part of the rental consideration. The Offeror should include a building space and parking plan indicating the location for the overnight GOV parking and general parking spaces reserved for the Government�s use. Facility Security Level (FSL): I (minimum) The Building must have an acceptable crime cast score as provided by FAA security. Buildings in high crime areas will not be considered. Operations Hours: 6:00 AM � 6:00 PM (with potential extension to 8:00 PM) Days: Monday�Friday The Government will not be amortizing Tenant Improvements (TI) as part of this procurement. The Government will reimburse the successful offeror for all tenant improvement costs within 90 days of substantial completion. The successful offeror will be required to fund this build out with no progress payments or any intermediate payments. The Government will confirm availability of funding for estimated total build out costs prior to lease award. This amount will be adjusted after Design Intent drawings have been approved by the Government, before the project is bid for construction and prior to any notice to proceed with Tenant Improvements. Evaluation Evaluation will be lowest-priced, technically acceptable, based on the lowest overall cost to the Government including but not limited to: total rent costs over 10 years, estimated build out costs reimbursed by the Government, estimated security costs paid by the Government as part of T/I reimbursement. If requirement details shift post-evaluation, the Apparent Successful Offeror may withdraw without penalty. This award is not finalized until a fully executed lease agreement has been signed by the Offeror and the Real Estate Contracting Officer on behalf of the US Government. How to Offer Please review the SFO Section 2 on How to Offer. The preferred method of response is email and electronic PDF but we will also except hard copies at our office address. There is no need to submit both an electronic and hard copy version. Offers received after the closing date and time will not be accepted. In the event of a Government shutdown that impacts FAA operations the deadline for responses will be extended once the shutdown has ended. Important Notes Please familiarize yourself with the terms of the FAA lease as the lease template varies slightly from the standard GSA template. Please note there is no firm term commitment included with this lease. Do not submit an offer and make assumptions that the FAA will renegotiate any lease terms if you are the apparent successful offeror. The FAA is not accepting offers for build to suit opportunities, this must be an existing building. The FAA is not accepting offers from individuals or entities that do not currently own the building and are attempting to secure an FAA lease award and then purchase or lease the building. You must be the current owner of the building or a brokers representative of the existing owner. If the FAA determines that you are not the building owner or a proper broker reprehensive for the building owner your offer will be immediately disqualified. You must be able to fund the FAA�s build out and tenant improvements. The FAA will reimburse the successful offeror within 90 days of substantial completion with a lump sum payment for all tenant improvements. There will be no progress or partial payments. You will be required to submit sufficient proof of financial ability to complete the build out. The FAA will not consider buildings in high crime areas, even though they might be in the search area. The building must have an acceptable crime cast score, generally below 200. The building must pass an FAA Security inspection prior to lease award. The apparent successful offeror will be required to submit the following environmental tests prior to lease award. Water test, Radon test on the first floor and any areas below grade, an asbestos report on any asbestos contained in the building, a certification of seismic compliance if the area of the country is a known seismic hazard area. Under no circumstances will the FAA reimburse any expenses incurred for the cost of responding to the Solicitation for offers. This includes the successful offeror and all non-successful offerors. title: 2026 Albuquerque Area IHS Native American-Owned Small Business Industry Day
description: ? Celebrating Our 6th Annual Industry Day � Connecting Native-Owned Businesses with Albuquerque Area Indian Health Service (IHS) ? Monday, September 28 & Tuesday, September 29, 2026 ? 9:00 a.m. � 3:00 p.m. Mountain Daylight Time (MDT) ? Virtual Event | Microsoft Teams ?? FREE to Participate ? Space is limited. Registration will close once all vendor presentation slots have been filled. The Albuquerque Area Indian Health Service (IHS), Division of Contracts and Grants Management (DCGM), invites Native American-owned small businesses to participate in the 2026 Albuquerque Area IHS Native American-Owned Small Business Industry Day, a two-day virtual event dedicated to strengthening partnerships, expanding the Albuquerque Area IHS supplier base, and increasing awareness of the capabilities of Native American-owned businesses. Held shortly before Indigenous Peoples� Day, this event provides Native American-owned small businesses, including eligible Small Business Indian Firms (SBIFs) and Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs), an opportunity to introduce their organizations and showcase their capabilities directly to Albuquerque Area IHS acquisition professionals, program stakeholders, and organizational leadership. ?? Event Overview Day One will begin with introductions from Albuquerque Area IHS acquisition professionals and a brief overview of the Buy Indian Act and its role in supporting Indian economic enterprises through federal procurement. Following the opening session, participating vendors will receive an individually scheduled 10-minute presentation slot to introduce their businesses and highlight their capabilities, qualifications, products, services, past performance, and other information relevant to potential Albuquerque Area IHS requirements. Vendor capability presentations will continue throughout both days. ? Vendor Capability Presentations This is your opportunity to show Albuquerque Area IHS what your business can do! Each participating vendor will receive 10 minutes to present its capabilities directly to Albuquerque Area IHS personnel and other invited IHS acquisition and program professionals. Vendors are encouraged to use their presentation time to highlight information such as: Core capabilities and areas of expertise Products and/or services offered Relevant experience and past performance Geographic areas served Unique capabilities or solutions How your business can support IHS healthcare operations and mission requirements ? Who Will Be in the Audience? The Industry Day is designed to connect Native American-owned businesses with Albuquerque Area IHS personnel and other invited IHS acquisition and program professionals involved in identifying requirements, conducting market research, planning acquisitions, making purchases, and administering contracts. The audience may include: Buyers Contract Specialists Contracting Officers Contracting Officer�s Representatives (CORs) Government Purchase Cardholders and Approving Officials Service Unit Chief Executive Officers Program and technical personnel Albuquerque Area leadership This broad audience provides participating businesses an opportunity to increase awareness of their capabilities across IHS while helping acquisition and program personnel identify potential sources for future requirements. ? Why Participate? The Albuquerque Area IHS is committed to meaningful industry engagement and expanding opportunities for Native American-owned small businesses. Participation in Industry Day provides businesses an opportunity to: Introduce their company directly to IHS acquisition, program, and organizational personnel Increase awareness of their products, services, and capabilities Help IHS identify new and emerging industry capabilities Support IHS market research and acquisition planning Develop relationships with acquisition and program personnel Increase awareness of potential opportunities to do business with IHS At the same time, these interactions help Albuquerque Area IHS broaden its procurement base, identify qualified sources, increase competition, and strengthen relationships with the Native American-owned business community. We want to learn what your business can do for IHS. ? How to Participate Native American-owned small businesses interested in participating should email: ALBAreaSmallBusiness@ihs.gov Please indicate your interest in participating in the 2026 Albuquerque Area IHS Native American-Owned Small Business Industry Day and include your business name and primary point of contact. Upon receipt of your email, the Albuquerque Area IHS will provide a registration form to collect additional business information and assist with scheduling. Presentation times will be scheduled in advance. Each participating vendor will receive 10 minutes to present its capabilities, qualifications, products, and/or services. Space is limited, and registration will close once all available vendor presentation slots have been filled. Vendors are encouraged to register early. Additional event and Microsoft Teams information will be provided to registered participants prior to the event. ? Building Partnerships in Support of the IHS Mission Through the 2026 Albuquerque Area IHS Native American-Owned Small Business Industry Day, DCGM seeks to strengthen relationships with Native American-owned businesses, expand awareness of industry capabilities, broaden the Albuquerque Area procurement base, and identify qualified sources capable of supporting healthcare delivery. These partnerships help ensure that Albuquerque Area IHS acquisition professionals have access to capable and innovative businesses that can provide the supplies, services, equipment, and solutions necessary to support direct patient care and advance the IHS mission: �To raise the physical, mental, social and spiritual health of American Indians and Alaska Natives to the highest level.� ? Join us September 28-29, 2026, and show Albuquerque Area IHS what your business can do! ?? Important Notice This Industry Day is being conducted for informational, outreach, and market research purposes. This event is not a bidder�s conference, solicitation, Request for Proposal, Request for Quote, promise to contract, or commitment by the Government to award a contract. Participation in this event does not guarantee consideration for or award of any future procurement. The Government will not assume liability for costs incurred by any participant associated with attending the event or preparing, submitting, or presenting information, capability statements, presentations, or other materials. Costs incurred in response to this notice will not be considered allowable direct or indirect charges to the Government.

description: La solvencia técnica o profesional deberá acreditarse, mediante la aportación de la titulación académica del personal directivo de la empresa. Además, la empresa licitadora deberá aportar copia del contrato de trabajo y de los TC1 y los TC2. Las empresas licitadoras habrán, por tanto, de contar en su plantilla con los profesionales indicados en el plazo de finalización de presentación de ofertas y mantenerlos en dicha plantilla durante la totalidad del plazo de duración de la concesión.

title: Netherlands – Laboratory, optical and precision equipments (excl. glasses) – Supply and Analysis of NH₃ Passive Samplers (Diffusion Tubes) for the MAN Network and additional projects
description: This European tender concerns a contract for the supply and laboratory analysis of ammonia (NH₃) passive samplers (diffusion tubes) for the Dutch ammonia monitoring network “Meetnet Ammoniak Nederland” (MAN) and various additional projects. The contractor will be responsible for the monthly supply of unexposed diffusion tubes to RIVM, the analysis of exposed tubes supplied by RIVM, and the digital reporting of validated results. Field deployment, return logistics of exposed tubes and internal data processing by RIVM fall outside the scope. The expected annual volume ranges from approximately 6,600 tubes in the baseline MAN scenario up to around 9,900 tubes including additional projects, with a maximum bandwidth of up to 30,000 tubes per year to accommodate future growth. If the contract is awarded to a new supplier, the first contract year will include a structured Double Measurement Programme, in which the new laboratory’s performance is systematically compared with the current trend laboratory to ensure continuity and trend stability in the MAN data series. The contract is tendered as one single, integrated lot combining tube supply, analysis and reporting with one contractor, using a best price‑quality ratio award criterion. The agreement has a fixed initial duration of six (6) years starting 1 January 2027, with five (5) optional one‑year extensions, for a maximum total duration of eleven (11) years.

title: Norway – Construction work – Temporary framework agreements for the procurement of compound tradesman services.
description: Oslobygg KF needs to establish a temporary framework agreement for compound trade services. The background for the procurement is an ongoing dispute relating to the ordinary procurement of a framework agreement for compound tradesman services. As a result of the dispute, the implementation of the ordinary procurement is pending. Oslobygg has a continual and significant need for trade services connected to the operation, maintenance and development of the company's property portfolio. It is therefore necessary to ensure sufficient capacity and continuity in the service delivery until the ordinary framework agreement can be established. Based on this, Oslobygg is carrying out a temporary procurement of compound trade services. The framework agreement shall cover Oslobygg ́s temporary needs and will i.a. include service assignments, ongoing maintenance and major maintenance projects where there may be a need for coordination of several trades. The framework agreement will be valid for 9 months, with an option for Oslobygg to extend the contract for a further 3 months. The total maximum agreement period is therefore 12 months. The temporary framework agreement is intended as a transitional solution up until the situation connected to the ordinary procurement has been clarified and the new ordinary framework agreement can come into force.
